textbookText: Section 'C' Short answer type questions. 1. What is the main reason of keeping maize in monocotyledon class? Write any two main causes. Ans:- The main reason of keeping maize in monocotyledon class are i. Parallel venation on leaves. ii. Fibrous root system 2. Classify fern plant and write two important characteristics. Ans:- Division: Pteridophyta. Characteristics: i) Have vascular tissues (xylem and phloem). ii) Reproduce by spores, not seeds. 3. Identify the division/phylum/class of the followings organism on the basis of their salient features: a)The body is covered with spiny skin and moves with tube feet. Ans:- Phylum Echinodermata. b) The body is covered with water proof scale and respire through gills. Ans:- Class Pisces (Chordata). c) The body is divisible into head, thorax and abdomen and can transfer malaria diseases. Ans:- Phylum Arthropoda (Insecta). d) The body have hollow tube, tentacles and stinging cells. Ans:- Phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria). 4. Why is angiosperm more developed than gymnosperm? Give two reasons. Ans:- Angiosperm more developed than gymnosperm because i) Seeds are enclosed inside fruits. ii) Presence of double fertilization. 5. Differentiate between bird and bat on the basis of two features. Ans:- Difference between bird and bat on the basis of features are,
wings formed by skin between fingers.

10. Fucus and Marchantia look alike, but Fucus is classified as algae while Marchantia is classified as bryothyta. Why?
Ans:- Fucus is classified as Algae due to absence of alternation of generations and vascular tissue, while Marchantia is
classified as Bryophyta because it shows alternation of generations and has a gametophyte-dominant life cycle.

1. The body of tapeworm is segmented but it doesn't belong to the phylum annelida, why? Classify the following organisms
Ans:- The body of tapeworm is segmented externally (pseudo-segmentation) but lacks true segmentation with internal septa
and organ systems like annelids. Hence, it belongs to Phylum Platyhelminthes, not Annelida.
